properties.title: Wildfire with IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for Scott and along the Caddo-Canadian County Line.
properties.description: At 1303  a large and destructive wildfire was burning out of control in northern Caddo County near Scott  spreading east-northeast rapidly. Wildfires can damage or destroy structures and can harm or kill people and animals. For your safety  EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY towards State Highway 37 to the north.
properties.instruction:
Those between CR 2670 and CR 2690/S Mayberry Road and SW 74th and CR 1130 should LEAVE this area NOW to avoid injury or death. Do not delay to pack belongings. 
Roads in the area may be impacted by fire and smoke. Never drive into heavy smoke. SLOW DOWN & MOVE OVER for emergency vehicles.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 15 at 1:49PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 149 PM AST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Utuado, moving westward at 5 to 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and small size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Jayuya, Adjuntas, Lares, Sabana Grande, San Sebastian, Utuado, San
German, Penuelas, Hormigueros, Mayaguez, Anasco, Las Marias, Cabo
Rojo, Santo Domingo, Monte Grande, La Playa, Puerto Real and
Maricao.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.
properties.area: Central Interior; Ponce and Vicinity; Northwest; Western Interior; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Southwest

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued September 15 at 1:38PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from St. Augustine to Flagler Beach FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL from 20 to 60
NM...
Waters from St. Augustine to Flagler Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

At 137 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a shower, capable of producing
winds to around 30 knots. This shower was located 9 nm east of
Jacksonville Beach, or 25 nm north of Saint Augustine, moving west at
20 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

Waterspouts are possible with this activity. If a waterspout occurs,
move your boat away from it. Waterspouts can develop rapidly and
produce winds and seas that are dangerous for vessels and everyone
onboard.

properties.description:

rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Guam...

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

additional heavy showers and thunderstorms. This may cause urban
and small stream flooding.

flooding.

Yona, Hagatna Heights, Andersen AFB, Talofofo,
Mongmong-Toto-Maite, Sinajana, Inarajan, Asan, Merizo, Piti,

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 9:58AM MDT until September 15 at 1:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Babylon burn scar in...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 100 PM MDT.

* At 958 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Babylon Burn Scar. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Babylon Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Babylon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central San Juan County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 9:49AM MDT until September 15 at 12:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 1245 PM MDT.

* At 949 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central San Juan County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become life
threatening in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams
or creeks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Immediately climb to higher ground. Runoff concentrated through
narrow canyon walls can quickly become dangerous, life threatening
conditions.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 15 at 7:31AM AKDT until September 15 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 715 AM AKDT, river gauges in Bethel have detected a rise in
water level above 8.5 feet. River gauge reports indicate rises in
water levels from the Kuskokwim River back-up in combination with
heavy rain across the advisory area. This is causing minor
flooding from overflow of poor drainage areas, especially along
the Kuskokwim.
- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the
ability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.
This has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into
Bethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough
and flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the
Kuskokwim.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 6:50am the stage was 8.6 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.
At 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.
At 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along the Kuskokwim River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.
